BESI.AS.balance_sheet: Net cash ~EUR153M ($175M): cash EUR509M vs debt EUR356M (convertibles). No leverage concern; funds buybacks/dividends through cycle.
BESI.AS.consensus_view: Post Q2-26 consensus: Q3-26 revenue guided +10-15% q/q at 63-65% GM; sell-side models ~23% revenue CAGR over next 3 years with net margin expanding ~30% to ~34%, implying roughly EUR550-700M net income by 2028 (estimated from Simply Wall St aggregation). Hybrid bonding: 2026 customer qualifications, 2027 volume production for HBM4/logic; 20+ HB customers. Avg price target EUR295 (~28% upside). HSBC is a notable dissenter seeing downside risk.
BESI.AS.summary: Thesis is confirmed by the just-reported Q2-26 (Jul 23): revenue EUR249.9M +68.7% yoy, orders EUR292.9M +128.8% yoy, H1 orders EUR562.6M +116.5% with ~60% AI-tied, net income EUR89M +177% yoy - hybrid bonding is inflecting into HBM4/logic mass production on the 2027 ramp. Market cap EUR18.2B (~$20.7B at 1.138 EUR/USD), price EUR229.90, up 83% in 52 weeks. Valuation is demanding: ~40x forward P/E (NTM net income ~EUR450M/$510M derived from mcap/forward P/E, estimated), 87x trailing, ~60x trailing EV/EBITDA - the order inflection is substantially priced. Short interest not published for the Amsterdam line (reported as -1). Net cash balance sheet and 63-65% gross margins support a premium 2036 exit multiple ~22x for a duopoly toll on stacking intensity, but entry multiple leaves little room for a 2028 digestion cycle.

GEV.balance_sheet: Net cash ~$9.0B ($12.7B cash vs $3.7B debt), and negative-working-capital model where customer down payments on the $176B backlog fund growth. No leverage concern.
GEV.consensus_view: Consensus 2026 EPS $14.99, 2027 EPS $24.38 (+63%), 2028 ~$30-33 (extrapolated from ~28% 3-yr EPS growth forecasts, estimated). 2026 guidance just raised: revenue $45.5-46.5B, FCF $11.5-12.5B (from $6.5-7.5B). Management on track for $200B backlog in 2027. Consensus assumes gas turbine pricing/mix keeps expanding Power margins and Electrification data-center orders compound; Wind stays a drag (Q2 orders -40%, -$275M EBITDA).
GEV.summary: Thesis fully corroborated by Q2-26 (Jul 22-23): orders +88% yoy to $24.2B, backlog $176B en route to $200B in 2027, FCF guide raised to $11.5-12.5B exactly as the thesis states, revenue $11.1B (~+20% yoy, estimated vs Q2-25). Market cap $274.6B (price ~$1,030), net cash $9B. The issue is price: ~48.5x NTM P/E (NTM earnings ~$5.7B derived from mcap/forward multiple), ~69x 2026 consensus EPS of $14.99, falling to ~42x on 2027's $24.38 - a huge earnings ramp is already underwritten, and the stock is +88% in 52 weeks. Short interest 4.4% of float. A 2036 terminal multiple of ~20x is defensible for a sold-out oligopoly grid/power equipment franchise, but current multiple implies most of the 2027-2030 slot value is in the price; the trailing P/E (29.5x) and EV/EBITDA (88.5x) screens are distorted and per-source figures conflict, so forward consensus is the reliable anchor.

VST.balance_sheet: Net debt ~$19.9B ($20.6B debt, $0.66B cash), roughly 2.6-2.9x 2026 guidance EBITDA of $6.8-7.6B - manageable for a hedged merchant fleet but rate-sensitive; $1.5B buyback authorization remaining.
VST.consensus_view: 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance $6.8-7.6B reaffirmed; consensus 2027 adjusted EPS $11.44 (+23% yoy) after ~$9.3 in 2026 (estimated); management targets >$10B cash generation through 2027 with continued dividend growth and buybacks. Q2-26 (reports Aug 7) consensus: EPS $2.43 +141% yoy, revenue $6.42B +51% yoy. Strong Buy, avg PT $223 (~32% upside).
VST.summary: Market cap $57.0B at $168.98 (Jul 23), forward P/E ~18.7x (other sources 17.5-18.0x), NTM earnings ~$3.05B (derived from mcap/forward P/E), trailing EV/EBITDA 11.7x. The valuation-arb leg of the thesis is directionally intact but narrower than stated: VST trades ~18x forward vs CEG at ~24-26x (not 26-32x), so the spread is ~6-8 turns, not 10-14. Growth is real - Q2-26 consensus revenue +51% yoy (expected, reports Aug 7; latest reported quarter growth is lower) and 2027 EPS growing 23% to $11.44. Net debt $19.9B (~2.7x EBITDA) vs CEG's cleaner balance sheet partially justifies some gap. Short interest 5.06% of float. Terminal multiple for a 2036 DCF should be ~13x - merchant nuclear/gas scarcity rents compress once new gas capacity arrives 2029-2031.

NRG.balance_sheet: Net debt ~$23.2B ($23.4B debt, $0.18B cash) after funding the LS Power deal - ~4.2x the $5.575B 2026 EBITDA midpoint. This is the key risk: leverage is elevated post-deal and deleveraging depends on hitting the $2.8-3.3B FCFbG guide; trailing GAAP EPS is only $0.87 (P/E 165x) due to deal amortization and hedge marks.
NRG.consensus_view: 2026 guidance (updated Feb 2026 post-close): adjusted EPS $7.90-9.90 (mid $8.90; consensus $9.05), adjusted EBITDA $5.325-5.825B, FCFbG $2.8-3.3B, reflecting ~11 months of the acquired fleet. Consensus 2027 EPS $11.31 (+27%), with 2028 mid-teens growth assumed from full-year LS Power contribution, 445MW of contracted data-center deals ($70-90/MWh, 10-20yr) scaling toward 1GW+, and the 5.4GW GEV/Kiewit newbuild JV (estimated). Strong Buy, avg PT $188.86 (~18% upside).
NRG.summary: Thesis event has closed: the 13GW LS Power gas portfolio plus CPower VPP completed Jan 30, 2026, and 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised ~$2.1B to a $5.575B midpoint - consistent with buying existing capacity below replacement cost while 2027-delivery newbuild is sold out. Market cap $30.2B (~$153/share), forward P/E 13.8x (NTM ~$2.18B adjusted earnings derived from mcap/forward P/E; note GAAP trailing earnings are near zero), the cheapest multiple in this group with 27% consensus 2027 EPS growth. Offset: net debt $23.2B (~4.2x EBITDA) makes this the most levered name here, so the scarcity-value thesis carries balance-sheet beta. Latest-quarter revenue growth ~12% yoy (estimated; TTM revenue $32.4B). Short interest 3.85%. Terminal 2036 multiple ~12x for a levered merchant/retail hybrid.

POWL.balance_sheet: Net cash ~$543M ($545M cash, ~$2M debt) - essentially debt-free with a large customer-advance float; no balance-sheet risk.
POWL.consensus_view: Consensus expects backlog conversion to drive FY27-FY28 acceleration: FY26 EPS estimates conflict across sources ($13.71 consensus / $14.80 Roth on what appears to be a pre-adjustment share base vs ~$5.8 NTM implied by the current forward P/E - treat per-share figures cautiously, aggregates are reliable), with ~15-18% 3-yr EPS growth forecast and 14.3% 3-yr revenue growth. The >$400M mega data-center order (largest in company history, awarded after Q2, runs through FY2028) hits Q3 backlog. Price targets scattered: $312 consensus, ranges $227-473.
POWL.summary: Backlog thesis confirmed: Q2 FY26 (Mar-qtr) orders $490M +97% yoy, backlog $1.8B +33% yoy, book-to-bill 1.7x for both Q2 and H1, plus a >$400M data-center mega-order landing in Q3 that extends visibility through FY2028. But current P&L lags the order book badly: revenue $296.6M only +6% yoy and EPS $1.25 down 1% yoy on higher comp/R&D. Market cap $8.83B with net cash $543M, trading ~47x trailing and ~42x forward earnings (NTM net income ~$210M derived from mcap/forward P/E) and ~36x EV/EBITDA - a small cap already priced for flawless backlog conversion, roughly triple its historical mid-teens multiple. Short interest 7.74% of float, the highest in this group, signaling a crowded debate on margin conversion of fixed-price backlog. Suggested 2036 exit multiple ~15x for a cyclical electrical-equipment fabricator.

TSM.balance_sheet: Fortress net cash: NT$3,518B cash/marketable securities vs NT$864B long-term debt as of Q2'26 — net cash ~NT$2.02T (~$69B USD). Self-funds ~$50B+/yr capex incl. $100B Arizona expansion from a 55%+ net margin.
TSM.consensus_view: FY26 revenue growth guided 'slightly above 40%'; FactSet consensus EPS NT$129.97 (2027) and NT$163.26 (2028) = 27.4% EPS CAGR 2026-28. 2027 wafer price hikes of 5-10% across all nodes (incl. first mature-node hike in 3+ years) are agreed with customers, with 10-15% premiums for incremental HPC capacity beyond original commitments.
TSM.summary: Q2'26 (reported Jul 16): record revenue NT$1,270.4B (~$40.2B USD), +36% YoY, with all-time-high 67.7% GM and 60.3% OM; net income NT$706.6B (+77% YoY), EPS $4.31/ADR; advanced nodes 77% of wafer revenue. Market cap ~$2.18T at ~19.5x forward (stockanalysis 19.45x; GuruFocus shows 25.3x on a different estimate vintage — NTM net earnings ~$112B implied, consistent with ~$89B 2026E and ~$115B 2027E net income). Thesis checks out on every number: GM 67.7% confirmed, 2027 price hikes locked, net cash ~$69B, short interest only 0.48% of float. The multiple is roughly market-level for a company compounding EPS at ~27% with monopoly economics on N2 and CoWoS; main risks are Taiwan geopolitics and the fact that the stock fell ~15% in early July despite record results (crowding/rotation risk). NTM earnings figure is my estimate derived from market cap / forward P/E, cross-checked against FactSet 2026-27 consensus.

MU.balance_sheet: Net cash: $26.0B cash vs $6.4B total debt (D/E 0.06, current ratio 3.4), plus >$22B of customer commitments ($18B upfront cash deposits) flowing in from SCAs. Balance sheet is the strongest in company history.
MU.consensus_view: FY27 consensus EPS ~$112/share (up from $90 in March 2026 — estimates rising fast); FQ4'26 guidance $50B revenue, 86% GM, $31 EPS. Management and consensus see the market tight through at least 2027, with 16 take-or-pay SCAs (~$100B RPO at MINIMUM volumes/pricing, ~5-yr terms) covering ~20% of DRAM and ~1/3 of NAND volume through 2030.
MU.summary: FQ3'26 (Jun 24): revenue $41.5B, +346% YoY and +74% QoQ, record 84.9% GM; FQ4 guided to $50B/86% GM/$31 EPS — stock ~$990, market cap ~$1.12T. Forward P/E is 6.9x on stockanalysis NTM basis (implying ~$162B NTM earnings, which the $31/qtr guide run-rate supports); on the slightly stale FY27 consensus of $112 EPS (~$127B) it's 8.8x — either way the thesis's 6-7x claim is in the right zip code, and GuruFocus shows 5.5x. Thesis validated and then some: $100B take-or-pay RPO confirmed, HBM4 ramping 2x faster than HBM3E ($1B+ shipped already), calendar-2026 HBM fully sold out, $22B customer prepayments. Key risk is that these are peak-supercycle margins (85%+ GM in memory is unprecedented) being capitalized at a low multiple precisely because the market doubts durability; the SCA floor-price structure is untested through a downturn. NTM earnings is an estimate (mcap/forward P/E); short interest 2.81% of float.

000660.KS.balance_sheet: Net cash position: KRW 3.8T net cash as of Q3'25 (interest-bearing debt KRW 24.1T), and with Q1'26 alone generating KRW 37.5T operating profit the net cash pile has grown materially since (exact mid-2026 figure not disclosed pre-Q2 print). Leverage is not a concern.
000660.KS.consensus_view: Wide dispersion: NH I&S forecasts 2026/2027 operating profit of KRW 289.4T / 470T won; Korea Investment & Securities cut 2026/27 estimates 9%/11% in July (arguing fixed-price HBM contracts cap upside) but kept a ₩3.8M target; brokers' targets cluster ₩3.8-4M vs ~₩1.8M share price. Q2'26 results due July 28. HBM demand exceeds supply capacity for the next three years per management; 2026 HBM sold out.
000660.KS.summary: Q1'26: revenue KRW 52.1T (+144% YoY) with a staggering KRW 37.5T operating profit (72% OM); market cap ~$923B after a brutal July — the stock hit ₩2.34M on July 2 then suffered its worst Seoul session on record July 13 (-12%) when a local broker argued fixed-price HBM contracts limit earnings upside. My NTM net earnings estimate is ~$140B (bracketed by KIS-cut consensus and NH's KRW 289T 2026 OP forecast; net income roughly 72-75% of OP given Korea tax), putting it at ~6.6x forward — within the thesis's 5.8-8x claim, and the cheapest of the five per earnings dollar. HBM leadership (~60%+ share, HBM4 ramping, 3 years demand>supply) is confirmed, but note the thesis risk just demonstrated: take-or-pay/fixed-price contract structures cut both ways, capping upside capture vs spot-exposed Micron. All NTM figures are estimates — Korean consensus is in flux ahead of the July 28 Q2 print; short interest % of float not reliably findable for KRX (KRX short-sale balance data not accessible), reported as -1.

AVGO.balance_sheet: Net debt ~$30B against ~$130B+ annualized adj. EBITDA run-rate building through FY26 — leverage ~1.0x net debt/EBITDA (down from 1.3x a year ago) and de-levering fast. VMware-era debt ($66B gross at peak) is no longer a constraint.
AVGO.consensus_view: FY26 AI semiconductor revenue guided to $56B (+~180% YoY); management reaffirmed FY27 AI revenue >$100B (~59% of ~$169B total consensus revenue), with six custom-ASIC customers locked; some analysts model $150B+ AI revenue by FY28. Street models ~52-53% revenue/adj-EBITDA CAGR FY25-28. Consensus 'Strong Buy' (27 buy/4 hold), avg target ~$524 (+36%).
AVGO.summary: FQ2'26 (Jun 3): revenue $22.2B +48% YoY, non-GAAP EPS $2.44 +54%, non-GAAP GM 77.1%; AI semis $10.8B +143% YoY (68% of semi sales) with FQ3 AI guided to >$16B (+200% YoY). Market cap ~$1.83T at 24.4x forward (~$75B implied NTM net earnings — my estimate from mcap/forward P/E). The $73B 18-month AI backlog and >$100B FY27 AI revenue line-of-sight are both confirmed company statements, and the 75%+ GM custom-ASIC/networking model is intact; balance sheet is now a non-issue at ~1.0x levered. It is the most expensive of the five (24.4x vs TSM 19.5x, NVDA 21x) and infrastructure software grew only ~13% with some VMware renewal fatigue noted — you are paying up for the highest-certainty backlog. Short interest 1.47% of float.

NVDA.balance_sheet: Net cash ~$40B ($53.2B cash vs $12.8B total debt) after generating $96.7B FCF in FY26 (+59% YoY); funding large buybacks plus strategic ecosystem investments (OpenAI/Anthropic-style commitments). No leverage concerns whatsoever.
NVDA.consensus_view: FY27 (ends Jan '27) consensus revenue ~$391B, EPS ~$9.34; FY28 consensus revenue ~$480-492B, EPS ~$11.43. Q2 FY27 guided to $91B ±2% (zero China DC compute assumed). Rubin begins contributing FQ3'27 with full-year Rubin consensus ~$38B; SemiAnalysis (Jun 30) argues 2H FY27 DC compute could beat Street by ~20% on the Rubin mass-production ramp. Strong Buy, avg target ~$303 (+45%).
NVDA.summary: Q1 FY27 (Apr '26): record revenue ~$81.6B (+~85% YoY, +21% QoQ — sources vary slightly on the exact print, $75-82B range across summaries; SEC 8-K headline $81.6B), Q2 guided $91B; TTM revenue $253.5B, TTM EPS $6.53. Market cap $5.06T at $208.76, forward P/E 20.95x → ~$241B implied NTM net earnings (my estimate from mcap/forward multiple, consistent with blended FY27 $9.34 / FY28 $11.43 consensus EPS). Thesis arithmetic verified: ~21x forward does embed deceleration (FY27 +54% rev growth vs +85% current run-rate, FY28 +23%), so if accelerator TAM is 2-4x consensus the stock is cheap even as the world's largest company; Rubin ramp timing and the $91B Q2 guide are near-term catalysts, and SemiAnalysis sees 2H upside. Risks: 1.33% short interest confirms it's a consensus long (crowding), China DC revenue is assumed at zero (option value, but also policy risk), and hyperscaler custom silicon (AVGO's $73B backlog) is nibbling at the training/inference mix. Long stance is coherent but it's the least differentiated of the five claims.

6501.T.balance_sheet: Net cash ~JPY 670B (~$4.5B): total cash JPY 1.68T vs total debt JPY 1.01T. No leverage concerns; funds $6B Hitachi Energy capex program plus buybacks from operating cash flow.
6501.T.consensus_view: FY2026 (ending Mar-2027) company guidance: revenue JPY 11.1T (+5%), adjusted EBITA JPY 1,420B (+8%), Lumada revenue JPY 4.8T (+16%). Hitachi Energy backlog of $57.9B (~3x segment revenue) gives multi-year visibility; sell-side (consensus Buy, avg PT JPY 6,036, +24% upside) models high-single-digit group EBITA growth through FY2028 with Energy margin expansion as +60-80% repriced transformer backlog converts and $1.5B+ capacity additions come online 2027.
6501.T.summary: Mcap JPY 21.77T (~$147B at ~148 JPY/USD, estimated conversion); trades ~23.9x forward, 27.5x trailing earnings. FY2025 (ended Mar-2026): revenue JPY 10.59T +8% yoy, record adjusted EBITA JPY 1.31T, net income JPY 802B; the thesis asset Hitachi Energy grew revenue 26% to $19.8B with orders of $32.8B and backlog swelling to $57.9B, and is adding US capacity (Canduct acquisition, $457M South Boston large-power-transformer plant broke ground June 2026). NTM consensus earnings ~JPY 910B (~$6.15B, derived from forward P/E — estimated). Conglomerate structure dilutes the transformer purity (Energy is roughly one-quarter of group), but valuation is undemanding for the quality and net-cash balance sheet.

LITE.balance_sheet: Roughly balance-sheet neutral: $3.17B cash vs $3.31B total debt (largely convertible notes), i.e., ~$141M net debt per stockanalysis — effectively no leverage risk, but converts add dilution overhang at these prices.
LITE.consensus_view: Consensus FY2026 (ends Jun-2026) EPS ~$5.26; FY2027 consensus EPS $18.07 (+121% yoy) on revenue +86%, with FQ1-27 revenue est $1.13B (+112% yoy) — estimates rising over the past 60 days. Management guided FQ4-26 revenue $960M-$1.01B and expects EML unit volumes +50%+ by the Dec-2026 quarter; sell-side effectively underwrites sold-out EML/CW laser capacity with price increases through 2027-2028.
LITE.summary: Mcap ~$64.9B after a ~700% one-year run; 52.2x forward earnings but only ~19x FY2027 consensus EPS of $18.07 if the ramp lands. FQ3-26 (Mar-2026): revenue $808M +90% yoy, non-GAAP EPS $2.37, gross margin +540bps qoq, 200G EML revenue more than doubled sequentially. NTM earnings ~$1.24B (derived from forward P/E — estimated). Thesis of sold-out EMLs with double-digit price increases is confirmed by management commentary, but 12.5% short interest, hyperscaler order concentration, and the fact the stock now capitalizes FY2027 hypergrowth mean scarcity rent is substantially priced; entry price matters far more than in early 2025.

CLS.balance_sheet: Modest net debt $564M ($942M debt vs $378M cash), well under 0.5x EBITDA against ~$959M TTM net income — no leverage concern; company continues buybacks.
CLS.consensus_view: 2026 guidance (raised twice): revenue $19B (+53%) and adjusted EPS $10.15 (+68%). Management set a 2027 revenue floor of at least $25.5B; consensus models ~$26.9B (+41%) with 2027 EPS in the ~$13-14.5 range (estimated from growth rates; explicit consensus not disclosed in sources). Drivers: 1.6T CPO Ethernet switch program ramping 2027, expanded US capacity for Google TPU systems; 21 analysts, consensus Strong Buy. Q2 earnings due July 27, 2026.
CLS.summary: Mcap $38.4B at ~$336/share; ~33x 2026 guided EPS of $10.15 and ~29.5x blended-NTM earnings of ~$1.30B (derived from forward P/E — estimated), so the thesis's '36x' is now closer to 30-33x after the stock's pullback-and-recover. Q1 2026 revenue grew 53% yoy and guidance was raised $2B to $19B revenue / $10.15 EPS; 2027 revenue floor $25.5B (+34% minimum) makes PEG well under 1 — genuinely the cheapest growth in AI networking hardware. Risks are structural not valuation: ODM economics (~6-7% operating margin), extreme hyperscaler concentration, and 2027 numbers already assuming flawless CPO/800G transitions. Short interest only ~3.3% of shares outstanding.

MP.balance_sheet: Net cash ~$690M ($1.74B cash vs $1.05B debt, mostly converts), bolstered by DoD's $400M equity stake and Apple's $200M prepayment — fully funds the 10X magnet facility buildout into 2028.
MP.consensus_view: Consensus has MP near breakeven in 2026 (forward P/E ~162x on ~$50M NTM earnings — derived, estimated) inflecting to 2027 EPS ~$1.06 (~42x 2027), though 2026/2027 estimates were revised DOWN over the past 90 days on China-truce pricing fears. The real earnings story is 2028+: 10X facility commissioning 2028 at 7,000 t/yr magnets, all under the 10-year DoD $110/kg NdPr floor + 100% offtake and the $500M Apple recycled-magnet deal; GM qualification underway.
MP.summary: Mcap $7.95B (~$44/share, down ~55% from the ~$100 late-2025 high, confirming the thesis's entry setup). Q1 2026: revenue $90.6M +49% yoy (plus $42M PPA income; $132.9M combined), record NdPr output of 917t (+63%), adjusted EPS $0.03 — first positive quarter. Current-year earnings are negligible (TTM net loss $71M; NTM ~$50M, estimated), so the stock is a 2028-2030 magnet-capacity bet valued on the DoD floor and offtake contracts rather than multiples. Net cash $690M derisks the build, but 18.6% short interest — highest among $2B+ materials names — reflects a live bear case that a durable China rare-earth truce guts ex-floor pricing and third-party magnet economics.

6268.T.balance_sheet: Net cash JPY 23.4B (~$160M): JPY 80.6B cash vs JPY 57.2B debt. Clean balance sheet funding the RV-reducer capacity doubling; dividend yield 1.66%.
6268.T.consensus_view: FY2026 (Dec year-end) company guidance: revenue JPY 327B (+6.2%), operating margin 8.5% (~JPY 27.8B OP); forward P/E 25.8x implies consensus net income ~JPY 22.9B. Sell-side is modestly constructive (5 buy / 1 sell, avg PT JPY 5,318 vs ~JPY 4,771-5,089 price) and models precision-reducer recovery through 2027 on auto/semi robot capex plus early humanoid orders, with RV capacity doubling completing in 2026; some quant frameworks flag the shares as ~19% above P/E-based fair value after the humanoid-theme rerating.
6268.T.summary: Mcap JPY 590.7B (~$4.0B at ~148 JPY/USD, estimated conversion); 25.8x forward and 36.4x trailing earnings — still a fraction of Harmonic Drive's (6324.T) ~100x+ theme multiple, supporting the relative-value leg of the thesis. Q1 FY2026 (Mar-2026 quarter): sales JPY 83.0B +16.9% yoy with operating profit +68% to JPY 8.2B, precision reduction gears the largest growth contributor (+JPY 4.8B) on auto/semiconductor robot demand recovery; ~60% global RV-reducer share confirmed, capacity doubling by end-2026. NTM earnings ~JPY 22.9B (~$155M, derived from forward P/E — estimated). Watch items: stock already rerated within a 52-week range of JPY 2,603-6,113 on the humanoid theme, group operating margin is only ~8.5% (reducers subsidize weaker segments), and Chinese RV/harmonic entrants are undercutting on price.

SHA.DE.balance_sheet: Net financial debt EUR 5.14B (~$6.0B) at Q1 2026, leverage 2.2x EBITDA - elevated post-Vitesco acquisition; FY26 FCF before M&A guided only EUR 100-300M, so deleveraging is slow. EV is roughly 1.7x market cap, meaning equity is a leveraged play on margin recovery.
SHA.DE.consensus_view: 10-21 analysts, consensus Buy but average PT only EUR 9.41 (~+4% upside; range 6.50-13). FY26 guidance confirmed: revenue EUR 22.5-24.5B (roughly flat vs EUR 23.5B in 2025, which declined 3.4%), EBIT margin before specials 3.5-5.5% (Q1'26 came in at 5.0% vs 4.7% prior year). Consensus models EPS recovery of ~90-95%/yr off the depressed 2025 loss-making base. Management: humanoid robotics revenue only 'two-digit million euros' in 2027, three-digit millions by 2030 at the latest - i.e., immaterial to group P&L before 2029-2030.
SHA.DE.summary: Market cap $8.68B (price ~$9.19, 945M shares, +58% over 1yr - the rerating has already started, stock is NOT at 52-week lows). Trailing P/E is negative (2025 restructuring/Vitesco losses); Q1'26 net income was just EUR 60M (EPS EUR 0.06) as EUR 5.1B net debt eats EBIT via interest expense. My NTM net income estimate of ~$0.5B (EUR 400-500M) is an estimate constructed from the 3.5-5.5% EBIT margin guidance less financial costs - implies ~17x NTM P/E, NOT the 6-8x in the thesis; the cheapness claim only works on EV/EBITDA (~5x on ~$14.7B EV vs ~EUR 2.4B EBITDA) or on 2027-2028 recovery EPS. Humanoid portfolio is real (planetary gear actuators launched at CES 2026, Hexagon Robotics strategic supply partnership, Humanoid Inc. deal to deploy hundreds of robots in own plants, actuators = ~50% of humanoid BOM with 25-30 per robot) but management itself guides to only tens of millions EUR revenue in 2027. Short interest not reliably published for the German float (-1). Sources: companiesmarketcap.com, schaeffler.com Q1'26 interim statement, stocksguide.com, investing.com.

SYM.balance_sheet: Pristine: $2.01B cash vs $28M total debt (net cash ~$2.0B, ~8% of market cap), operating cash flow $845M TTM helped by customer deposits/deferred revenue. No leverage concern; the Altman Z-score flag on screeners is an artifact of the deferred-revenue-heavy model.
SYM.consensus_view: 19 analysts, consensus Buy, avg PT $65.67 (+62%). FY26 (Sept FY): revenue $2.79B (+24%), EPS $0.51; FY27: revenue $3.51B (+26%), EPS $0.58. Q3 FY26 guide $700-720M revenue, $80-85M adj EBITDA. Consensus assumes mid-20s% revenue growth through FY27-28 with adj EBITDA margin expanding from ~11-12% toward mid-teens as software/services mix grows; GreenBox JV and Walmart Mexico/international expansion are the 2027-2028 optionality.
SYM.summary: Market cap $24.45B at $40.57 (602.7M aggregate share count incl. Class V units). Thesis facts check out with corrections: contracted backlog $22.7B confirmed, GAAP profitability confirmed but razor-thin (Q2 FY26 net income $9M on $676M revenue, +23% YoY; TTM GAAP net income still -$7.4M), and the drawdown is -24% H1 2026 / -17.9% over 52 weeks - not -35% YTD. NTM earnings ~$0.35B is a proxy derived from the 70.3x forward P/E (stockanalysis.com); on GAAP EPS this is a 70-80x forward name, so the long is a growth/backlog-conversion story, not a value story. Gross margin only 20.4% (systems installation-heavy) with operating margin ~breakeven at -1.1%. Short interest is high at 14.5% of float - crowded short, squeeze fuel but also signals persistent skepticism on Walmart concentration (~85%+ of revenue) and past accounting restatement history. Acquired Arms Innovations July 2, 2026 for micro-fulfillment. Sources: stockanalysis.com, fool.com, simplywall.st.

MSFT.balance_sheet: Fortress: $78.2B cash vs $125.4B total debt - modest ~$47B net debt against ~$125B TTM net income; capex of ~$190B calendar 2026 is pressuring FCF but is fundable from operating cash flow. No leverage concern; watch finance-lease buildup for data centers.
MSFT.consensus_view: 58 analysts, Strong Buy, avg PT $556.75 (+46% - the widest consensus upside among US megacaps). FY26 (ended June 30, 2026, reports ~July 29): revenue $329.6B (+17%), EPS $16.83 (+23%). FY27-28: consensus 3-yr revenue CAGR 17.4%, EPS CAGR 18.1%, implying FY27 EPS ~$19-20. FQ4 guide was $86.7-87.8B revenue (+13-15%), Azure +39-40% cc, capex >$40B/qtr. Sell-side debate is entirely capex/depreciation drag and Copilot seat monetization pace, not demand.
MSFT.summary: Market cap $2.83T at $381.58, down 24.5% over 12 months - thesis drawdown confirmed, and 20.6x forward P/E (NTM EPS ~$18.5, NTM net income ~$137B est) is the cheapest MSFT has traded relative to the market in years (trailing 22.7x vs 12-mo avg 30.7x). Fundamentals show zero demand deterioration: FQ3 2026 (Apr 29) revenue $82.9B +18% (beat), EPS $4.27 +23%, Azure +40%, AI run-rate $37B +123% YoY, and capex actually came in $3.4B BELOW consensus at $31.9B. The bear case is gross margin compression (67.6%, lowest since 2022) from data-center depreciation and OpenAI relationship/accounting complexity, not distribution or share loss. Short interest 1.2%. Imminent catalyst: FY26 Q4 earnings ~July 29-30, days after trade entry. Sources: stockanalysis.com, gurufocus.com, cnbc.com, investinglive.com.

GOOGL.balance_sheet: Net cash ~$130B ($242.5B cash vs $112.8B debt) - the self-funded compute thesis holds, but FCF went NEGATIVE (-$5.9B in Q2 2026) on record $44.9B quarterly capex; also formed a $25B TPU infrastructure JV with Blackstone to move some build off balance sheet. Balance sheet can absorb $195-205B 2026 capex, but the cash pile will shrink materially.
GOOGL.consensus_view: 64 analysts, Strong Buy (44 SB/14 B), avg PT $430.89 (+36%). 2026: revenue $489.1B (+21.4%), EPS $14.26 (+31.9%). 2027-2028: consensus extrapolates high-teens revenue growth on Cloud (backlog $514B, Cloud revenue +82% YoY to $24.8B in Q2'26 with 35.6% operating margin) with EPS growth moderating as depreciation catches up. Key consensus assumption: capex peaks as % of revenue in 2026-27 and Cloud margin keeps expanding.
GOOGL.summary: IMPORTANT thesis correction: the '15.9x trailing' P/E is real on screeners but badly distorted - TTM net income of $244B on $446B revenue (54.8% net margin) includes enormous non-operating/unrealized investment gains; on operating earnings GOOGL trades ~22x forward (2026 EPS $14.26 at $317.69; NTM net income ~$175B is my estimate bridging 2026/2027 consensus). Also, this is no longer a beaten-down name: +66% over 52 weeks, $3.89T market cap. Q2 2026 (July 22): revenue $119.8B +24%, operating income +30% to $40.8B, Cloud +82%, but stock FELL on capex guide raised to $195-205B and -$5.9B FCF. TPU full-stack, Waymo (~500K rides/week) and DeepMind assets are real and consensus-acknowledged. Short interest 0.79%. The long here is paying a market-plus multiple for the best-capitalized AI full-stack - fine, but the 'cheap' leg of the thesis does not survive scrutiny. Sources: stockanalysis.com, biggo.com/investing.com Q2 coverage, cnbc.com, seekingalpha.com.

FCX.balance_sheet: Solid: $4.08B cash vs $10.36B total debt, net debt ~$6.3B (<1x EBITDA at current copper prices); EV $97.6B. Operating cash flow $2.0B in Q2 alone. Main balance-sheet-adjacent risk is the Indonesian smelter obligations and eventual Grasberg ownership step-down to Indonesian government interests (2041 horizon).
FCX.consensus_view: 23 analysts, Buy, avg PT $71.20 (+12%; range $30-82, bulls at $77-81 on $3.40 NTM EPS x 24x). 2026: revenue $29.0B (+12%), EPS $2.83 (+60%). 2027-2028: consensus assumes Grasberg Block Cave ramp completes (volumes recover from the Sept 2025 mud-rush disruption), copper stays $5.50-6.00+/lb, driving EPS toward $4+ in 2027. Note stock slipped after Q2 as management's copper outlook commentary softened.
FCX.summary: Market cap $91.3B at $63.50 (+38.7% over 52 weeks - copper thesis is substantially recognized already; Comex averaged $6.32/lb in June 2026 vs ~$4.20 two years ago). Q2 2026 (July 23) beat: adj net income $1.1B / $0.74 EPS vs $0.62 est, revenue $7.03B vs $6.71B est - but revenue is ~-7% YoY (my estimate) because Grasberg volumes are still down (~786M lbs produced, 710M lbs sold at $6.17/lb realized, unit cash cost $1.97/lb); price is doing all the work. Trailing P/E 31.1x, forward ~19.2x (NTM EPS ~$3.20 est, NTM net income ~$4.6B est) - this is NOT statistically cheap for a miner; it is a bet that consensus copper deck is too low and Grasberg recovery adds volume torque into a structural deficit. Cleanest large-cap copper claim is fair (85%+ revenue from copper, US-listed, Tier 1 assets, US smelting/leach optionality benefits from Section 232 tariff regime). Short interest 2.16%. Terminal 12x reflects historical 10-14x large-miner exit range. Sources: stockanalysis.com, benzinga.com, tipranks.com, sec.gov 8-K, seekingalpha.com.

EQT.balance_sheet: Total debt $5.7B, net debt $5.5B at Q2'26, down from $7.69B at YE2025 and approaching the $5B target; investment grade; UBS sees ~$2B of buybacks possible in 2027 once the target is hit. Owns midstream (Equitrans) giving structurally lowest cost basis in Appalachia.
EQT.consensus_view: Strong Buy consensus (24-25 analysts, PT $67.12-67.72, ~26% upside). CY2026 revenue consensus $9.32B (+13.9%); CY2027 EPS consensus $4.29 (range $2.62-$6.38), implying ~12.4x 2027. EIA July STEO: Henry Hub avg $3.67 for 2026, $3.37 Q3'26 — i.e., consensus already assumes gas recovers off the current ~$2.83-2.93 spot. Sell-side models debt paydown 2026, capital returns 2027, LNG/power demand inflection 2027-28 (EQT signed 500kt/yr LNG offtake starting 2028, ~$45M FCF add).
EQT.summary: Price $53.39, mcap $33.4B (Jul 23, 2026). Trailing P/E 12.4 (TTM EPS $4.31, flattered by hedge/one-time gains), forward P/E 14.9 implying NTM EPS ~$3.6 / NTM net income ~$2.2-2.3B (estimated from the multiple; sources conflict on whether the $4.29 consensus is 2026 or 2027 — WallStreetZen tags it 2027). Q2'26 beat operationally despite $2.89/MMBtu realized gas: FCF $330M in the quarter, $2.16B YTD, capex 9% under guide, and 2026 production guidance raised ~90 Bcfe to 2,375-2,450 Bcfe. The long thesis's core fact pattern checks out: spot HH was $2.83 on Jul 13 vs EIA forecasting $3.67 avg 2026, and the company is levered to 2027-28 power/LNG demand — but note the market is not fully asleep: 24 of 25 analysts already rate it Buy and the stock rallied on the Q2 print (Jul 22). Short interest ~3.8% of float (Dec 2025 reading, stale).

U-UN.TO.balance_sheet: No debt. Closed-end physical trust holding 81,497,348 lb of U3O8; total NAV US$7.13B (Jul 23, 2026). Can only issue units via ATM when trading at a premium, so the current discount freezes new buying by the trust itself. Recently raised US$25.55M via non-brokered private placement.
U-UN.TO.consensus_view: No EPS consensus (physical trust). Uranium market consensus is structurally bullish: term price hit $91.50/lb in Q1'26 (+$11.50 yoy) vs spot $85.25-85.75/lb in July; primary mine production covered only ~89% of reactor requirements in 2024 with secondary supplies largely exhausted; Goldman Sachs projects ~2.3B lb cumulative U3O8 shortfall 2025-2045 and Sprott projects a 197M lb deficit by 2040. Sprott/ETF Trends flag 2026 as a demand-inflection year on restarts, SMR orders and hyperscaler PPAs.
U-UN.TO.summary: P/E is meaningless — current_multiple shown is price/NAV of 0.90 (market US$18.73 vs NAV US$20.72/unit, a -9.58% discount as of Jul 23, 2026, confirming the thesis's 9.6%). Mcap ~$6.45B USD (344M units × $18.73); NTM 'earnings' are just the management expense drag, estimated ~-$35-45M/yr (~0.5-0.6% MER, estimate). The trust holds 81.5M lb U3O8 worth $7.13B with spot at ~$85.50/lb and term at $91.50/lb. The thesis's supply/demand frame is directionally supported (2024 mine supply = ~89% of reactor requirements; note the specific '197Mlb' figure appears in Sprott materials as the cumulative deficit by 2040, not annual requirements — annual requirement is ~180-200Mlb vs ~155-165Mlb mine supply, consistent). Key mechanical caveat: the discount can persist indefinitely (it has since 2024) since there is no redemption mechanism at NAV; suggested terminal 'multiple' is 1.0x NAV. Short interest not findable (-1).

WTKWY.balance_sheet: Net debt €4.04B (~$4.7B), roughly 1.8-2.0x EBITDA (estimated) — comfortable for an 85%-recurring-revenue business; TTM operating cash flow €1.67B, FCF €1.36B, and the company continues buybacks/dividends.
WTKWY.consensus_view: Consensus Buy from 15 analysts, avg PT €91.70 (+53% from €59.76). FY2026 guidance reaffirmed May 6: organic growth ahead of prior year, adjusted operating margin ~28.0%, high-single-digit adjusted EPS growth in constant currency; Q1'26 organic growth was 5%. Sell-side models ~4.5% 3yr revenue CAGR and ~9.3% 3yr EPS CAGR through 2028. Morningstar cut the moat to narrow and FVE to €120 on AI disruption risk (JPMorgan flagged Anthropic's finserv agent tools as the trigger for the early-2026 selloff) but still calls the stock undervalued.
WTKWY.summary: WKL at €59.76, mcap €13.32B ≈ $15.6B (at ~1.17 EUR/USD, estimated), down 56.5% over 12 months and ~65% from peak on AI-disruption fears — this is a genuine fallen angel, not a quiet mispricing. Trailing and forward P/E both ~10.6x (TTM EPS €5.64; NTM net income ~€1.26B ≈ $1.5B estimated), matching the thesis multiple; note the thesis's '21% NI growth' is well above the ~9% 3yr EPS CAGR consensus actually models — the 21% likely reflects a one-year IFRS figure, so underwrite HSD growth instead. Business quality intact so far: Q1'26 organic +5% (accelerating vs FY25), 85% recurring revenue, cloud software +14% organic, ~28% margins, and guidance was reaffirmed post-selloff. The bet is precisely the thesis's claim: whether regulated-workflow content (UpToDate clinical, CCH tax) survives AI reading primary sources — Morningstar keeps a narrow moat medium-term but won't vouch for 20 years, which argues for a discounted terminal multiple (~12x suggested vs historical ~25x). Short interest not disclosed on European listing (-1). Next earnings Aug 5, 2026.

ADP.balance_sheet: Fortress: ~$3.4B long-term debt (estimated), one of the few AA-rated US corporates, effectively net-cash excluding client-fund obligations; ~$35B average client float generates a growing interest-income stream that cushions revenue if headcount stalls.
ADP.consensus_view: Consensus Hold (18 analysts), PT $254 (+4.6%) — sell-side is already lukewarm. FY26 (ends June 2026) guidance raised in April: revenue +6-7%, adjusted EPS +10-11% (~$11.05); consensus NTM/FY27 EPS ~$11.95, and 2026-2028 models assume ~5-7% revenue and ~8-10% EPS growth continuing. Critically for the short thesis, consensus already embeds only ~1% pays-per-control growth (Q3 FY26 actual: +1%) — i.e., near-zero US employment growth, not employment decline. FY26 Q4 report due July 29, 2026.
ADP.summary: Price $242.88, mcap $97.1B (Jul 24, 2026), trailing P/E 22.7, forward P/E 20.3 on NTM EPS ~$11.95 → NTM net income ~$4.8B (estimated from multiple × ~400M shares). The multiple has already compressed hard — the stock is down ~20% over 12 months (mcap -20.5%) while EPS grew 10%, so the market is partially pricing the AI/white-collar risk; short interest is 3.5% of float but up 184% yoy, meaning the crowd is arriving. Q3 FY26 (Apr 29): revenue +7% (+6% organic cc), adjusted EPS +10% to $3.37, EBIT margin 30.2%, pays per control decelerated to +1%. The short thesis's transmission mechanism (0.7-1.0 revenue elasticity to white-collar headcount) is plausible but consensus already assumes ~1% pays-per-control and only ~6% revenue growth, and the float income + AA balance sheet + 2.8% dividend slow the bleed; 20x is rich only if EPS growth breaks below ~5%. Earnings catalyst July 29.

PAYX.balance_sheet: Carries ~$5B of debt from the 2025 Paycor acquisition (estimated; ~$4.2B notes issued) against roughly $1.5B corporate cash — a change from its historically debt-free profile, leverage ~1.5x EBITDA (estimated). Still returned $2.2B to shareholders in FY26; dividend yield now 4.3% with a high (~85-95% GAAP) payout ratio.
PAYX.consensus_view: Consensus Hold, PT $108.50 — 2% BELOW the current $110.66 price; sell-side is already bearish-neutral. FY27 guidance (given Jun 24, 2026): revenue +5-6%, adjusted EPS +7-9% (implies ~$5.90-6.00 vs FY26's $5.51), adjusted operating margin ~44%; the stock slid on this cautious outlook. Consensus 2027-2028 assumes SMB employment roughly flat and Paycor synergy capture driving the margin — the guide does embed 'SMB stability,' as the short thesis claims, but with only ~5% organic growth assumed, not heroic numbers.
PAYX.summary: Price $110.66, mcap $39.4B, 355.7M shares (Jul 24, 2026). Trailing GAAP P/E 22.6 (TTM EPS $4.89, depressed by Paycor amortization — confirms thesis figure) but forward P/E is only 18.5 on NTM adjusted EPS ~$5.99 → NTM adjusted net income ~$2.1B (estimated); the stock is already down 23% yoy and trades below the consensus target. FY26 (ended May 2026): revenue $6.51B +16.9% (Paycor-inflated; Q4 +12%), adjusted EPS $5.51 +11%; FY27 guide of +5-6% revenue / +7-9% EPS was received as disappointing. Short interest 5.7-6.5% of float — this is a well-populated short with a 4.3% dividend yield cost-of-carry, so the easy multiple compression (from ~27x to 18.5x forward) has largely happened; incremental downside requires SMB payrolls actually contracting, which FY27 guidance does assume away. New ~$5B debt load and 44% margins on a slowing top line give the short more torque than ADP if AI-driven SMB headcount cuts materialize on the thesis's timeline.

ASML.balance_sheet: Strong net cash: EUR 7.6B cash and equivalents at end-Q2 2026 vs roughly EUR 4B gross debt (net cash ~EUR 3-4B, estimated); FCF EUR 1.3B in Q2 alone; returning cash via EUR 1.1B/quarter buybacks under a 2026-2028 program. No leverage concerns whatsoever.
ASML.consensus_view: 2026 guidance raised twice to EUR 43-45B revenue (vs ~EUR 32B in 2025, ~+35%) with 54-56% gross margin; ~65 low-NA EUV shipments in 2026 (+45% EUV net system sales yoy) and at least 80 guided for 2027, with +30% capacity for 2028 under evaluation. 2027 consensus EPS has surged to ~$49.46 (from $36.46), and UBS sits 10-15% above that. Year-end 2025 backlog was ~EUR 38.8B, exceeding all of 2025 sales; note ASML stopped publishing quarterly bookings from Q1 2026, making momentum harder to track.
ASML.summary: Market cap ~$692.5B (~$1,770/ADR, ~391M shares), forward P/E ~49.3x as of 2026-07-16 (GuruFocus 49.65, FinanceCharts 49.28), implying NTM consensus net income of ~$14B (estimated as mcap/forward P/E; FY2026 guidance of EUR 43-45B revenue at 54-56% GM arguably supports EUR 13-15B net income, so the 49x screen may rest on stale estimates and true NTM P/E could be nearer low-40s). Q2 2026: EUR 9.3B sales (+~21% yoy, estimated vs EUR 7.7B Q2 2025 base), 54.0% GM, EUR 2.9B net income, beat guidance. The long thesis has hard confirmation: guidance raised twice in 2026, 2027 EUV output effectively sold out, 2028 +30% capacity under study. Key risk is that 49x forward is roughly double ASML's 10-yr median multiple, so the monopoly rent is far from free; short interest not findable but historically ~1% (estimated).

CEG.balance_sheet: Post-Calpine (closed 2026-01-07, $21.8B total consideration incl. ~50M new shares and $12.7B assumed net debt): long-term debt $17.0B plus $5.1B short-term borrowings, so ~$20B+ net debt (estimated ~2.3x EBITDA). Management pledged to preserve investment-grade ratings; S&P raised Calpine to BBB+ as a core subsidiary. Leverage is real but manageable for a contracted-nuclear cash machine.
CEG.consensus_view: FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance affirmed at $11.00-12.00 on 361M diluted shares; management targets >20% base EPS growth 2026-2029 and 10%+ rolling 3-yr growth long-term, implying ~$14-15 EPS by 2028 (estimated). Sell-side is near-unanimously bullish: 14 buys / 1 sell, mean target $358 (~30% above the $275 price). Crane restart (MSFT PPA) back on track for 2027 after a June 2026 FERC waiver; Walmart added as a new long-term nuclear PPA counterparty.
CEG.summary: Trading ~$275.07 (2026-07-23), market cap ~$99.3B (estimated: $275 x 361M diluted shares; a $88.7B print circulating dates from the early-July $240-245 low). Forward P/E ~24x on the affirmed FY2026 guide of $11-12 adjusted EPS ($4.15B at midpoint; NTM ~$4.5B estimated given >20% growth targets) — notably BELOW the 26-32x premium band in the thesis, because the stock hit a 52-week low of $240.27 in early July before rebounding. Q1 2026 revenue roughly doubled yoy on Calpine consolidation (organic growth far lower); EPS beat and 20% growth framework reiterated. Short interest modest at ~3.2-3.6% of float (11.38M shares, falling). The contracted-scarcity-rent thesis is intact (Crane/MSFT on track for 2027, Meta Clinton, new Walmart PPA) and the entry multiple is now cheaper than the thesis assumed.

MAN.balance_sheet: Total debt ~$1.04B, debt/equity ~0.50, net debt roughly $0.4-0.6B (estimated); Q2 2026 FCF was -$9M (seasonal working-capital build, vastly improved from -$207M a year earlier). Balance sheet is adequate but cyclically sensitive; no near-term solvency issue.
MAN.consensus_view: Consensus FY2026 EPS ~$3.66 with recovery broadening into 2027-2028 (sell-side models mid-single-digit revenue growth and EPS marching toward $5+ by 2028, estimated); Q3 2026 guidance was issued alongside Q2. Analysts are chasing, not leading: UBS raised its target to $41 from $33 (Neutral) and the Street mean of ~$37.6 sits BELOW the ~$50-52 post-earnings price — the market has front-run the ratings.
MAN.summary: Market cap ~$2.43B after the stock exploded from $39.02 (7/15 close) to above $52 intraday on 7/16 (+34% on the day) following a Q2 2026 beat: adjusted EPS $0.99 vs $0.95-0.96 consensus, revenue $4.86B (+7.5% yoy, first broad recovery print). At ~$51, forward P/E is ~14x on FY26 consensus EPS of $3.66 (NTM earnings ~$0.17B, estimated). CRITICAL for the short thesis: short interest was already 13-20% of float (6.75M shares, ~19.9% per the 7/16 report), and Benzinga explicitly attributes part of the spike to a short squeeze — this is a crowded short that just ripped 34% against the bears, with a cyclical-recovery narrative now armed with beating numbers. The robotics-substitution short may be right on 2027-28 fundamentals but entry timing is dangerous: borrow is crowded, the tape has momentum, and the mean analyst target below spot shows sell-side capitulation-upgrades are still ahead as a squeeze fuel source.

6324.T.balance_sheet: Historically conservative Japanese balance sheet with modest debt and substantial cash/securities (net position roughly neutral to net cash, estimated — current-period detail not findable); no leverage concern. The concern is entirely valuation and margin structure, not solvency.
6324.T.consensus_view: Company FY3/27 guidance (issued ~2026-05-13): revenue JPY 68.0B (+14.2%), operating profit JPY 6.2B (+141.5%), net profit JPY 4.5B (+179.7%). Humanoid-related orders: ~JPY 2.5B booked in FY3/26 with management suggesting they could double or triple in FY3/27 on US prototype programs. Sell-side broadly parrots the physical-AI narrative ('world's No.1 precision reducer'); bears (e.g. ainvest) note revenue grows while profits collapsed and valuation ignores both. Chinese competitor Leaderdrive undercuts Harmonic's ~$800/unit ASP by 30-40% and supplies Tesla.
6324.T.summary: Stock JPY 6,570 (2026-07-21), market cap ~JPY 651B = ~$4.43B (at ~147 JPY/USD, estimated), up +143% over 12 months though down ~11% in the last week. The thesis's profit collapse is confirmed: FY3/26 net profit was revised to ~JPY 1.58-1.61B, down ~54% from FY3/25's JPY 3.47B, exactly matching the '404x trailing at net income -54%' setup (TTM P/E has since compressed to ~167x as Q4 profits recovered). Even on the aggressive FY3/27 company guide of JPY 4.5B net profit (+180%), the forward P/E is ~145x (NTM earnings ~$31M estimated) for a company guiding only +14% revenue growth — the multiple prices p90 humanoid volumes AND sustained pricing power while Leaderdrive sells 30-40% cheaper into Tesla. Humanoid orders are real but tiny: JPY 2.5B (~$17M, ~4% of revenue) in FY3/26, 'could triple' in FY3/27 — i.e., ~$50M of orders supporting a $4.4B valuation. Short interest not findable (Japanese disclosure differs; borrow may be tight after the +143% run). The Corning-2000 analogy holds quantitatively; main short risks are squeeze mechanics in a narrative stock and yen translation.

PLTR.balance_sheet: Large net cash position, no material debt — roughly $6-7B+ cash/short-term investments (estimated; latest 2026 figure not findable but the company has been strongly FCF-positive throughout). Zero solvency risk; the short case is pure valuation/commoditization, with no balance-sheet catalyst.
PLTR.consensus_view: FY2026 revenue guidance raised to $7.650-7.662B (~+71% yoy); consensus FY2026 EPS ~$1.32; consensus FY2027 revenue ~$11.22B (+46%), with sell-side illustrations of ~$2.31 FY2027 EPS at a 53% margin (a projection, not official consensus); FY2028 consensus extrapolates to roughly $15-16B revenue (estimated). Bulls (24/7 Wall St) argue $300B is 'only the start'; some targets reach $352 by end-2027. The consensus assumption is that agentic-AI demand keeps US commercial (+133% yoy in Q1) compounding with no commoditization of the integration layer through 2028.
PLTR.summary: Market cap ~$323.3B at ~$134 (2026-07-20), down ~33-35% from the January 2026 high and ~27% YTD — consistent with the thesis's -30%. Fundamentals are running HOTTER than the thesis credits: Q1 2026 revenue +104% yoy to $1.282B (first triple-digit print since listing), US commercial +133%, FY26 guide ~+71%. Valuation remains extreme even after the drawdown: ~42x the FY2026 revenue-guide midpoint (~55x trailing sales, estimated), forward P/E ~80x on NTM earnings of ~$4.0B (estimated blend of FY26 ~$3.4B = $1.32 EPS x 2.57B shares and FY27 ~$5.9B), and 200x+ trailing earnings. Short interest was only ~2.3% of float at the last findable print (Oct 2025 — stale; treat as low-single-digit), so this is not a crowded short, but shorting a company compounding at 70-100% requires the commoditization inflection to arrive before the multiple is grown into: at consensus 2027 revenue of $11.22B the stock is 'only' ~29x sales. Timing risk is severe; the -30% YTD move means some perfection is already deflated.
